title: Variance input
description: Input contract for the step-12 variance assessment (is the difference real?). It exists because statistics_input.schema.json cannot carry the four things step 12 needs: replicate structure, censoring flags, a frozen sigma reference and a pre-registered delta. Three data-quality rules are structural here, taken from the WGO_001 empirical lessons: (1) a censoring time is never an endpoint, so every censored observation must declare event_occurred / event_time / censoring_type and a non-empty stop_reason; (2) material identity must be verifiable, so every observation traces to sample_id + batch_id; (3) confounders must be excludable, so intervention windows are declared explicitly. Censoring is rejected fail-closed: an observation censored without a stop_reason is refused rather than estimated around.

analyses.description: Which step-12 analyses to run. VARIANCE_COMPONENTS is the nested decomposition, POWER_ANALYSIS the power / required-n block, CONSISTENCY_CHECK the same-arm replicate agreement rule.

replicate_structure.description: Declared nesting of the runs, one entry per level. The declared n is what the plan assumed; the engine reports it next to the observed counts so a shortfall is visible rather than silent.

observations.description: The runs being assessed. sample_id + batch_id are required on every entry: an observation that cannot be traced to a specific sample from a specific batch cannot be used as a replicate at all. event_occurred is required because same-arm outcome agreement is judged on it, and `at` is how an observation is tested against intervention windows.

at.description: ISO-8601 instant of the observation. Required in practice whenever a confounds=true intervention exists, because the engine must be able to prove the observation is outside the window.

event_occurred.description: Whether the failure event happened. Required: same-arm replicates that disagree here are REPLICATE_INCONSISTENT regardless of the numbers.

event_time.description: Event time when the event occurred; null when it did not. A censoring time is never recorded here.

censoring.description: One entry per observation whose outcome is unknown. stop_reason is required whenever censoring_type is not NONE, so a censored value can never be presented without its cause; a censored observation missing it is rejected fail-closed.

event_time.description: Null for a censored observation: the censoring time must not be recorded as an endpoint.

intervention_events.description: Non-protocol events that could confound the comparison. An entry with confounds=true defines a window [at, until]; observations inside it are flagged and excluded from the variance estimate. Omit `until` for an open-ended window, which is the conservative reading.

comparison_arms.description: The two arms whose difference is being judged. Omitted when only the nested decomposition is wanted; without it no difference can be claimed, and the verdict then cannot be NO_DETECTABLE_DIFFERENCE.

frozen_sigma_reference.description: Pointer to the step-5 method-characterisation record the frozen sigma came from. Sigma is an asset that accumulates from blank reference samples included in every round; step 12 compares against it and does not re-estimate it.

frozen_sigma.description: The frozen noise baseline imported from method characterisation. Preferred over the freshly estimated sigma for the power calculation, because estimating sigma needs an order of magnitude more data than using a known one.

control_band.description: Control band for the same frozen baseline, when the method is characterised by a band rather than a single sigma.

preregistered_delta.description: The smallest difference worth detecting, pre-registered at step 3 before the runs. Required in practice for POWER_ANALYSIS: without a pre-registered delta no power can be computed, and a design whose power is unknown cannot be declared free of a difference.

k_required.description: Frozen separation factor for SIGMA_MAX = delta / k. Defaults to 3. When k < 3 the design rule is NOT to add replicates but to change the method or the criterion.

resolution_n_values.description: Replicate counts to tabulate in the resolution table. Defaults to 2, 3, 6, 12 (the pack's step-12 table).
